lede: Buyers now ask AI engines who to shortlist. GEO is the work that decides whether your name is in the reply, and whether the facts are right.
answer: Generative engine optimisation (GEO) is the work of getting a brand named, cited and described accurately in AI answers from engines such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews. A GEO agency measures what those engines say today, finds the sources they trust, fixes the pages, reviews and press behind each answer, then re-measures every week.

sections.h2: What is generative engine optimisation?
sections.html:
Generative engine optimisation (also spelled generative engine optimization) is the practice of shaping what AI engines say when a buyer asks about your category. You will also see it called AI search optimisation, answer engine optimisation (AEO), LLM visibility or, informally, ChatGPT SEO. The goal is the same: be named in the answer, be cited as a source, and be described with facts that are true today.

SEO earns a position in a list of links. GEO earns a sentence inside the answer itself. The two share foundations, such as crawlable pages and clear structure, but GEO also depends on the third-party sources engines read: reviews, forums, Wikipedia, press and comparison lists. Read what generative engine optimisation is for the long version, or GEO vs SEO for a side-by-side view.

sections.h2: Why does GEO matter now?
sections.html:
Fewer searches end on your website. When Google shows an AI summary, people click far less, and almost nobody clicks the links inside it. B2B buyers increasingly start their research in an AI chat tool rather than a search box. If the answer does not name you, many buyers never reach a page where you could make your case.

The good news is that answers can be influenced with honest work. Research from Princeton and IIT Delhi found that content with statistics, quotations and cited sources is more visible in generative answers.

faqs.q: What is the difference between GEO and SEO?
faqs.a: SEO aims to rank a page in a list of search results. GEO aims to get your brand named and cited inside the AI-written answer. GEO builds on good SEO, but it also depends on reviews, forums, Wikipedia and press, because AI engines read those sources before they answer.

lede: Investors now ask AI engines about your company before they open your filings. We make sure the answer reflects your latest disclosures, not last year's.
answer: Investor relations GEO keeps what AI engines tell investors about a listed company accurate and current. It uses only public disclosures, follows SEBI rules and needs company sign-off before anything is published. The work strengthens the sources AI reads, such as filings, annual reports and call transcripts, and sets drift alerts so each new result replaces the old figures.

sections.h2: What does AI say about listed companies?
sections.html:
Ask an AI engine about a listed company and it will give a confident summary: revenue, margins, debt, management and recent news. That summary is stitched together from sources of very different ages. If the most-read sources are stale, the answer is stale, and it is delivered with the same confidence as a fresh one.

For an investor relations team this is a new kind of exposure. The answer is not on your website, you did not write it, and you may not know it exists. Investor relations GEO makes it visible, measures it every week and fixes the sources behind it.

items.d: Results, shareholding patterns and disclosures filed with the exchanges.
Long, rich documents that engines often read selectively, so the key figures must be easy to extract.
Management commentary that engines quote directly, sometimes long after it is out of date.
Business news coverage, which often outranks your own pages as a cited source.
Data and screener sites that restate your numbers, not always the latest ones.
Your Wikipedia article and investor forum threads, which can keep an old story alive.

items.d: The engine reports figures from an earlier year or quarter as if they were the latest.

items.t: A resolved controversy as the headline

sections.h2: How does investor relations GEO work?

items.d: We run the questions investors actually ask, across eight AI engines, and capture each answer with its date and sources.
We mark every claim as current, outdated or wrong, and trace it to the source the engine relied on.
We prepare fixes from public disclosures only: clear results pages, investor FAQs, schema, transcript pages and sourced Wikipedia talk-page requests.
Your company secretarial, legal and IR teams approve every item before anything is published.
We re-measure weekly and report accuracy, sources cited and sentiment against the Week-1 baseline.

sections.h2: What happens after each results announcement?
sections.html:
Results days are when AI answers drift most. New figures are filed, but engines keep quoting the old ones for a while. After each announcement we re-scan the investor questions and raise a drift alert wherever an answer still cites the previous period, a superseded figure or an outdated source.

Each alert comes with the source causing it and a proposed fix, ready for your sign-off. The same alerts run after other material events, such as a change in leadership or a large order you have disclosed.

Inside the lines: we use only information you have already disclosed publicly. We do not add forecasts, selective figures or promotional language, and we do not try to bury news that is accurate. The aim is an answer that matches your filings. Every item follows SEBI rules and needs company sign-off before it is published.

sections.h2: What changed in one investor relations programme?
sections.html:
For one listed company in India, the AI answer to common investor questions moved from old figures and a resolved controversy to the latest filing. Answer accuracy went up, current sources were cited more often, the old controversy stopped leading the answer, and investor sentiment in the answers improved.

See the before-and-after in the investor relations case study, illustrated with a fictional company, Meridian Industries. For the wider picture, read what happens when AI gets your brand wrong.

faqs.q: Is GEO for investor relations allowed under SEBI rules?
faqs.a: Yes, when it is done properly. We work only from information you have already disclosed publicly, add no forecasts or promotional claims, and publish nothing without your company's sign-off. The aim is accuracy, which is what disclosure rules are there to protect.

faqs.q: Why does ChatGPT still quote our old financial results?
faqs.a: AI engines answer from the sources they find and trust, and those are often older articles, portals or transcripts. If your latest figures are hard to extract or rarely cited, the old ones win. We make the current disclosures easy to find and quote, then measure whether the answers change.

faqs.q: Can you remove negative news about our company from AI answers?
faqs.a: No. We do not bury accurate news. If a matter has been resolved, we make sure the resolution and the current facts are documented in public sources, so an engine has what it needs to give a complete and current answer.

faqs.q: Who approves what you publish?
faqs.a: Your company does. Every page, FAQ, Wikipedia talk-page request and media note goes through your IR, legal and company secretarial teams before it is published.

faqs.q: How quickly do AI answers update after we announce results?
faqs.a: It varies by engine and source, and no one can force an update. We re-scan after each announcement, flag answers still quoting the previous period and fix the sources behind them. You see the gap close, or not, in the weekly report.

sections.html:
When someone asks an AI engine whether a company is reliable, the engine does not take your word for it. It reads what customers and journalists have written about you: Google reviews, category portals, marketplaces, forums and news. Your reputation becomes a sentence in the answer, positive or not.

That makes reviews and press a direct input to your AI visibility, not just a sales aid. A thin, old or unanswered review profile gives an engine little to work with, or the wrong things.

sections.html: What we never do: write fake reviews, pay people to pose as customers, post from fake accounts or make promotional Wikipedia edits. These tactics break platform rules and consumer advertising rules, and once found, they damage the trust you were trying to build.

sections.h2: How do you know reputation work is paying off?
sections.html:
We measure two things. First, the review profile itself: volume, recency, rating and the share of reviews with a reply. Second, what AI engines now say about you: the sentiment of each answer and which sources they cite. The Optimizer GEO platform records every cited review site and article, so you can see which ones move the answer.

Reputation also feeds the rest of the engine. Customers who leave detailed reviews are often the ones who join your community, and buyers who arrive after reading reviews show up in your pipeline data.

faqs.q: Do online reviews affect what ChatGPT says about my brand?
faqs.a: They can. AI engines read review sites, portals and forums when they describe a company, and they reflect the tone they find. A recent, well-answered review profile gives them accurate material to work with.

faqs.q: Can you delete negative reviews about my business?
faqs.a: We do not remove genuine reviews. We reply to them in public, fix the cause where we can and report reviews that clearly break a platform's own rules through the proper process. A thoughtful reply to a fair complaint often builds more trust than a spotless rating.

faqs.q: How can we get more genuine reviews without breaking the rules?
faqs.a: Ask real customers at the moment they are happiest, make it easy to leave a review on the right site, and never offer incentives that a platform prohibits. We set up that routine with your team and track how it performs each week.

faqs.q: Do you write or buy reviews?
faqs.a: No. We never write fake reviews or pay people to pose as customers. Besides being dishonest, it breaks platform and advertising rules and can undo years of trust.

faqs.q: How fast should a business reply to a bad review?
faqs.a: As soon as you can reply accurately and calmly. A quick reply shows other buyers you are listening, but a wrong or defensive reply does more harm than a short delay. Every reply we draft is checked and approved by your team.

answer: A feeder network is the set of channels a brand owns or earns that send buyers, and AI engines, back to it. Owned feeders include a blog, a guide site, a video channel, a newsletter and a WhatsApp channel. Earned feeders include creators, credible "best X in Y" lists and independent newsletters. sections.h2: What is a feeder network?
sections.html:
Most brands rely on one website and whatever paid reach they can buy. A feeder network spreads your presence across the places buyers already spend time, and where AI engines look for independent signals. Some of those places you build and own. Others you earn by being worth writing about.

Every feeder carries the same verified facts as your main site, so wherever a buyer or an engine meets you, the story is consistent. That consistency is what turns many small mentions into one clear picture.

That is a correlation, not proof of cause, but it matches what we see in the sources engines cite: they lean on places that talk about a brand, not only places that link to it.

faqs.a: Not always. If your main site can host a strong, well-structured guide section, that may be enough. A separate guide site makes sense when the topic is broader than your brand and deserves its own home, and it is always clearly marked as yours.

sections.h2: Why do communities and forums shape AI answers?
sections.html:
AI engines want to know what real people think, so they read forums. Reddit is now the most directly cited source across the major AI engines, and Quora threads appear often too. If the conversation about your category happens without you, the engine learns your category from someone else.

That does not mean flooding forums. It means showing up where your buyers already ask questions, as yourself, with answers that are genuinely useful.

items.d: Reddit is the top directly cited source across ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Gemini, Perplexity and AI Overviews.

Articles, guides and FAQs that settle a question in the first paragraph, written to be quoted.

sections.h2: How can a brand use Reddit without astroturfing?
sections.html:
Reddit marketing for brands works only when it is done openly. Our rules are simple:

  • Post from an account that is clearly the brand, never a fake customer.
  • Answer the question that was asked, with facts, even when the honest answer is not your product.
  • Follow each community's own rules, and stay out where brands are not welcome.
  • Never buy upvotes or coordinate accounts to push a thread.

In one real-estate programme, open answers in city and home-buying threads were part of what lifted the developer's AI visibility. More on the method in how to get cited by AI engines.

sections.h2: What does digital PR add to community work?
sections.html:
Communities show what customers think. Press shows what independent observers think. Engines weigh both. Our digital PR team pitches real stories, data and expert comment to trade and business media, and works to place you on credible "best of" lists and local guides.

Good coverage also strengthens your reputation and becomes part of your feeder network, sending readers back to you long after the story runs.
Posted openly, as the brand: no fake customers, no sock-puppet accounts, no paid posts disguised as opinion. If a community would object to knowing who wrote something, we do not post it.

faqs.q: Is it okay for a brand to post on Reddit?
faqs.a: Yes, if it is honest about who it is and follows each subreddit's rules. Many communities welcome clear, helpful answers from a labelled brand account. They do not welcome disguised promotion, and neither do we.

faqs.q: Will Reddit users just downvote a brand account?
faqs.a: Some will, especially if the reply sounds like an advert. Useful, specific answers that admit limits tend to be received far better. We also stay out of communities where brands are not wanted.

faqs.q: Who writes the content, AI or people?
faqs.a: Both. Content agents find questions and prepare first drafts from your verified facts. Our content team edits every piece, and your team approves anything regulated or sensitive before it is posted.

faqs.q: Should we build our own community or join existing forums?
faqs.a: Usually both. Existing forums are where buyers ask questions today and where engines read. A community on your own site is where loyal customers gather and where you control the space. We help you decide the balance for your category.

faqs.q: What is the difference between digital PR and paid media?
faqs.a: Paid media buys space, and the reader knows it is an advert. Digital PR earns coverage because the story, data or expert view is worth reporting. Engines treat earned coverage as an independent source, which is why it matters for AI visibility.

sections.h2: Why does reply speed decide which leads you win?
sections.html:
Interest fades fast. Research published in Harvard Business Review in 2011 found that companies replying to an enquiry within an hour were about 7 times more likely to qualify the lead than those that waited longer. Most enquiries do not arrive during office hours, and most sales teams cannot reply to all of them within the hour.

An AI agent replies in seconds, at any time, and hands your team a qualified lead with the conversation attached.

sections.h2: Where do the agents work?

items.d: A chat on your key pages that answers product, policy and process questions from approved facts and books the next step.
A WhatsApp AI agent that replies where many Indian buyers prefer to talk, and keeps the thread for your team.
Replies to direct messages from people who found you through posts, reels or creators.

sections.h2: What does an agent do in a conversation?

items.d: Uses only your verified facts, and says so plainly when it does not know.
Asks the questions your sales team would ask, such as need, timeline, budget range and location.
Offers a call or site visit and confirms the time with the buyer.
Passes the lead to the right person with a short summary, so nobody has to ask the same questions twice.

sections.h2: Why does accuracy matter more than a clever reply?
sections.html:
A chatbot that invents a price, a possession date or a feature does more damage than no chatbot at all. Our agents draw on the same fact pages we build for GEO, checked and approved by your team. If a question falls outside those facts, the agent says it will check and hands over to a person.

Regulated claims follow the same rules as the rest of our work: RERA, ASCI and SEBI checks before anything goes live, and data handling aligned with India's DPDP Act.

sections.h2: How do we set up an AI agent?

items.d: We collect and verify the answers buyers need: products, specifics, policies, locations and timings.
With your sales team we agree the qualifying questions, what counts as a good lead and when to hand over.
We run the agent against real questions from your own enquiries and fix every weak answer.
The agent goes live on the channels you choose, starting with the busiest.
We read conversations, update facts and tune the flow, and report bookings and qualified leads.

sections.h2: How do agents connect to the rest of the engine?
sections.html:
Every conversation is a record of what buyers actually ask. Those questions feed the prompt universe we use to plan GEO work, so your content answers the questions people really have. Each agent also asks, politely, where the buyer first heard of you, which feeds the first-touch data in leads and pipeline.

For sectors with high-value, considered purchases, such as real estate, booking the visit is often the moment that matters most.
What our agents won't do: pretend to be human, invent prices or availability, or push a buyer who has said no. Every agent says it is an AI assistant, and a person is always one step away.

faqs.q: Can a WhatsApp AI agent book site visits or sales calls?
faqs.a: Yes. The agent offers available slots, confirms the time with the buyer and passes the booking and conversation summary to your team. We agree the booking rules with you before launch.

faqs.q: Will an AI chatbot make up answers to customer questions?
faqs.a: Ours are built to answer only from facts you have approved. When a question falls outside them, the agent says it will check and hands the conversation to a person. We review conversations weekly to catch and fix weak answers.

faqs.q: Does the agent tell people it is an AI?
faqs.a: Yes, always. Buyers trust a clear AI assistant more than one that pretends to be a person, and honesty here matches how we work everywhere else.

faqs.q: What happens to customer data from the chats?
faqs.a: Data handling is aligned with India's DPDP Act. We agree with you what is collected, why, where it is stored and who can see it, and we collect only what qualification needs.

faqs.q: How is this different from a normal website chatbot?
faqs.a: Many chatbots follow fixed scripts or answer from whatever text they can find. Our agents work from verified facts, qualify against criteria your sales team set, book the next step, and feed what they learn back into your GEO and attribution work.

sections.h2: Why do most attribution reports miss AI search?
sections.html:
Buyers now do most of their research before they speak to you. They read AI answers, reviews and forum threads, and they rarely click through. When they finally arrive, your analytics records the visit as direct traffic or a brand search, and the source that convinced them disappears from the report.

That leads to a familiar mistake: cutting the organic work that created the demand, and crediting the last ad the buyer happened to click.

sections.h2: What do you do with attribution data?
sections.html:
You move money to what works. If buyers keep naming one guide or one review site, that feeder gets more investment. If a channel produces traffic but no pipeline, you can stop it with confidence. And when the board asks what organic marketing returns, you can show deals, not impressions.

The data also sharpens the rest of the engine. First-touch answers reveal new questions for GEO, and conversations from AI agents show which facts buyers needed before they booked. See what an AI visibility audit includes for the metrics behind the first scoreboard.

An honest note on method: no tool can see inside a private AI chat. Attribution for AI search combines what buyers tell you, tagged links and dated answer captures. It is strong evidence, not perfect certainty, and we show you how every number was built.

faqs.q: How do I track leads that come from ChatGPT?
faqs.a: You cannot see inside a buyer's chat, so you combine signals. Ask every new lead where they first heard of you, tag links from your owned channels, and line up enquiry trends with dated captures of what the engines were saying. Together these give a clear, defensible picture.

faqs.q: What is first-touch attribution?
faqs.a: First-touch attribution credits a deal to the place the buyer first met your brand, such as an AI answer, a review or a forum thread. It shows which channels create demand, while last-touch attribution only shows where buyers converted.

faqs.q: Does this replace our CRM?
faqs.a: No. We work with the sales records you already keep. We add the first-touch question, source tags and the link to AI answer data, and report from there.

faqs.q: Can organic lead generation replace paid ads?
faqs.a: Over time it can reduce how much you depend on them, because owned assets keep working when budgets stop. Most companies run both while the organic engine builds. Attribution shows you when the balance can shift.

faqs.q: How do I prove organic marketing ROI to my board?
faqs.a: Show closed deals traced to where demand began, alongside the AI answer and SEO scoreboards, all against a Week-1 baseline. That turns organic work from a cost line into a pipeline report.

faqs.q: How often is the data updated?
